# Incident Report — Network Forensic Analysis
**Case reference:** mta-2022-01-07
**Evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 frames), `exported_objects/`
**Analyst tooling:** tshark 4.x, `file`, `shasum`, `strings`

## 1. Victim / Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **192.168.1.216** |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (NetBIOS shows as `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2`, same host, transposed OCR-adjacent character in NBNS broadcast; DHCP option 12 confirms `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2`) |
| AD domain | `spoonwatch.net`, workgroup/domain tag `SPOONWATCH`, DC at 192.168.1.2 (`SPOONWATCH-DC`) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **steve.smith** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString` from 192.168.1.216 to the DC, alongside the machine account `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$`) |

Evidence: `dhcp.option.hostname`, `nbns.name`, `kerberos.CNameString` fields extracted directly from the capture.

## 2. Malware Family

**Behaviorally consistent with Vidar Stealer** (Arkei/Vidar-lineage info-stealer). **This is a behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed** — no Suricata/IDS alert export or AV/YARA detection was present in the evidence directory, only the pcap and HTTP-exported objects.

Basis for the attribution:
- HTTP POST requests use `multipart/form-data` with a fixed boundary (`1BEF0A57BE110FD467A`) and header `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` — a signature request fingerprint long associated with Arkei/Vidar-family stealer C2 traffic.
- The malware downloads seven numbered files disguised with `.jpg` extensions that are actually **PE32 DLLs**. `strings` analysis of each shows they are the legitimate third-party support libraries stealers fetch to read browser credential/cookie stores: `sqlite3` (SQLite, for Chrome/Edge cookie & login DBs), `nss3.dll`/`freebl3.dll`/`softokn3.dll`/`nssdbm3.dll` (Mozilla NSS, for Firefox password decryption), and the `vcruntime140`/`msvcp140` VC++ runtime the stealer binary depends on.
- The host then exfiltrates a ZIP archive to the same server, whose internal path structure (`autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Network.txt`) matches Vidar's known stealer-log folder layout (`autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, per-browser log files).
- No prior DNS lookup was made for the C2 IP, no delivery vector is visible in this capture window (the infection/execution occurred before or outside this recording), consistent with an already-running Vidar loader beaconing and exfiltrating.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control
- **2.56.57.108:80/tcp** (HTTP, plaintext) — sole C2 endpoint observed. No associated domain name; the client connects directly to the IP with no preceding DNS query, i.e. the C2 address is hardcoded in the malware.
- Check-in endpoint: `http://2.56.57.108/osk/main.php`
- Exfil endpoint: `http://2.56.57.108/osk/`

### Malicious domains
- None observed. All traffic to the C2 is by bare IP; DNS traffic in the capture resolves only to legitimate Microsoft/Windows Update/AD infrastructure (`download.windowsupdate.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `spoonwatch.net` AD zone, etc.), which is background noise and not part of the malicious infrastructure.

### Malicious URLs (payload downloads, all HTTP GET-equivalent POST to 2.56.57.108, response `200 image/jpeg`)
| URL | File type (actual) | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` | PE32 DLL (console) | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) — NSS `freebl3.dll`/`nss3.dll` | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg` | PE32 DLL (console) — `msvcp140.dll` | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) — SQLite3 | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) — SQLite3 | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg` | PE32 DLL (console) — `vcruntime140.dll` | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |

### Exfiltrated file (client → C2, POST `http://2.56.57.108/osk/`, 379,629 bytes)
- Filename in transfer (per `Content-Disposition`): **`_5861695120.zip`**
- SHA256: **`1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f`**
- Archive contents observed: `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Network.txt` — i.e. stolen Chrome/Edge autofill data, saved payment-card data, and session cookies from `steve.smith`'s profile.

## 4. Not indicators (ruled out)
The `am_delta_patch_*.exe` and `*.cab` transfers to `23.38.189.225`/`23.38.189.201`/`8.253.189.126` (`download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`) are legitimate Windows Defender/Windows Update Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization traffic, unrelated to the compromise.

## 5. Summary
Host **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as **steve.smith** on the `spoonwatch.net` domain, is infected with an info-stealer behaviorally consistent with **Vidar Stealer**. It beaconed to **2.56.57.108:80**, pulled down 7 support DLLs disguised as `.jpg` files, checked in at `/osk/main.php`, and exfiltrated a 379,629-byte ZIP of stolen Chrome/Edge autofill, card, and cookie data to `/osk/`. Recommend isolating the host, resetting `steve.smith`'s credentials and any stored browser passwords/cookies, and blocking 2.56.57.108.
